long_biography.plain_text:
Christian Candy brought shared residential services to a smaller collection of apartments and townhouses at 80 Holland Park. His plans addressed practical family needs alongside leisure facilities, including storage for pushchairs, dog-washing facilities and space for working or studying at home. The scheme reflected the surrounding neighbourhood's villa architecture.

Candy chose to complete and staff the development before offering its homes for sale, so buyers could assess the finished buildings and services. CPC assembled a team of architects and interior designers for the project, combining individual residences with a concierge, residents' lounge, swimming pool and gym.

uncertainties.detail: The active 80 Holland Park beneficial-owner entry supplies positive retained-asset evidence. Current portfolio proportions and Guernsey group ownership percentages are not established. UK CPC Group 09577977 is dissolved and CPC London 09411596 is in liquidation; neither is treated as proof that the Guernsey platform has ended or as current director evidence. The property sector and founder role use medium-confidence core-business inference.

The company website dates establishment to 2004 whereas the court chronology records Guernsey incorporation in 2003. Exact founding year is omitted from biographies. The grandmother's modest first-purchase loan is acknowledged but does not itself establish a substantial family-wealth platform; broad Self-made is used.

Christian's CPC and Nick's later Candy London, Candy Ventures and political roles are not interchangeable. The judgment explicitly declined to resolve the sole-beneficial-ownership dispute; no claim that a court established sole ownership is made.

The primary register confirms July 1974, not the day. Exact birth day and birthplace are not proposed on the available evidence. Existing Wikipedia link redirects to Nick and a correction to Christian is recorded for separate review. Searches of Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, TikTok, personal sites, Vimeo and Flickr returned coverage, namesakes or third-party photographs, not verified personal accounts.
